key_insight: Physics-informed ensemble learning identifies Mg alloys that improve strength or reduce cost and carbon emissions while accounting for real-world constraints.
engineering_relevance: The framework links alloy composition, microstructure, and processing routes to support material selection under performance, cost, and sustainability requirements.
method: Integrate structure–property physics with ensemble learning.
Predict properties and infer processing routes under sustainability constraints.
Screen millions of candidate compositions and microstructures in a digital alloy library.
evidence_signal: Trained on a benchmark dataset and validated for Mg alloys, the framework identified a rare-earth-containing solution with 72.8% higher yield strength and 61.1% higher tensile strength than same-family alloys at comparable cost and emissions, plus a rare-earth-free solution with 40.4% lower cost and 88.9% lower emissions than its primary-feedstock counterpart without compromising mechanical performance.
watch_item: Transferability beyond Mg alloys and robustness to variable feedstocks require further validation.
paper_title: Machine learning enabled design of sustainable alloys considering real world constraints
